subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram provider intermittently stalls despite stable direct Bot API connectivity

question: Should OpenClaw proactively repair the Telegram SOCKS/proxy transport path now, or require a fresh current-main live repro before changing shared proxy and fallback semantics?
rationale: The source path and Undici contract make the SOCKS proxy failure plausible, but the available fix directions affect compatibility-sensitive shared proxy behavior and still lack current live Telegram proof.

options.title: Sponsor Shared Proxy Repair
options.body: Own a scheme-aware explicit and env proxy fix with focused tests and require redacted live Telegram getMe/sendMessage proof before merge.

options.title: Wait For Live Repro
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer code changes until a reporter or maintainer reproduces the SOCKS5 stall on current main or a current release.

options.title: Limit To Documentation
options.body: Decline transport changes for now and document supported DNS/proxy workaround paths, leaving the runtime behavior unchanged.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Shared Proxy Repair
recommendation.body: Own a scheme-aware explicit and env proxy fix with focused tests and require redacted live Telegram getMe/sendMessage proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are listed for the Telegram subsystem and have nearby fallback-chain history in the affected transport path.
